Expanding ||v+w||_4^4=1 gives T=-(1+6R)/4; Cauchy--Schwarz gives (1+6R)^2<=32R(1+R), hence R>=5/2-sqrt6. The real quartic identity then gives A^4+B^4=24-12R<=2(6sqrt6-3). Power mean and Cauchy--Schwarz yield the M1 and M2 bounds. Independent exact symbolic evaluation of the stated two-coordinate witness verified all three unit constraints, R=5/2-sqrt6 and A^4=B^4=6sqrt6-3, so both bounds are attained. Absolute convergence of the coordinate sums follows from v^2,w^2 in ell_2, so the argument applies to arbitrary index sets with at least two coordinates.
